newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BAe to move A$50 mln work to Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BAe to move A$50 mln work to Australia.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc's (BAe) Australian subsidiary said on Monday its parent would award A$50 million of defence contract to Australian companies, including itself.

"British Aerospace will award A$50 million worth of defence contracts to Australian companies following its success last month in securing a number of major UK contracts," British Aerospace Australia said in a statement.
A spokeswoman for British Aerospace Australia said the British contracts meant more work could be redistributed.
She declined to nominate which companies might gain the work, apart from British Aerospace Australia itself.

The British government said in July that British Aerospace would be contracted to provide the Royal Air Force with heavily upgraded Nimrod patrol aircraft and the Storm Shadow stand-off ground-attack missile.
Last week, British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo confirmed that Britain would buy 232 Eurofighter 2000 aircraft, a European project in which British Aerospace is a partner.
